original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Finite verification inside the masked (E-graph) model of PR1212: for every 7-subset X of P112 (242802 orbits under the 8-generator FRAME0-stabiliser subgroup H, covered by a four-level candidate chain with explicit transporters in H), is there a pivot frame F inside P112 \ X satisfying PR1560's frame-incidence criterion (D), (G), (W) and the nonempty-block premise of its Corollary 2? If so, PR1560's written theorem makes every P105 unit rigid. Extends PR1616 (P107, P106) by one level.
scope_change_reason: Revision 3 retired the complex-masked-decoder card into this one, keeping masked supports as an allowed method, and this card's gate requires a masked support to change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound. This package is a side result on that requirement: with PR1560, an exact eight-costly-term masked decoder on any P105 live set is rigid (an all-pairs decoder up to gauge), so masking does not escape PR968's floor at p = 15. It builds no decoder, prices no profile and does not address child rank.
bottleneck_link: Side result, not a lever: it closes the masked eight-costly-term route for p <= 15 (floor 57 = 72 - 15 at P105 through PR1212 section 8; 56 = max(72 - p, 56) takes over at p >= 16). No kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop at P105 with every unit verified exactly; a structural (D)/(G) lemma and nine or more costly terms are left open.
evidence: verify.py --cover: 13 exact checks (model and the frame identity (6) on all 2025 frames; generators; H rebuilt in breadth-first order, 172032 elements; triple orbits; four-level candidate coverage: 2517 quadruple candidates onto 180 representatives, 18782 5-subset candidates onto 1614 units, 156627 6-subset candidates onto 19295 units, 1651528 7-subset candidates onto 242802 P105 units, each candidate the image of its unit under an indexed element of H; PR1560's fixture and control; (G) and (D) each fail on deficient frame families of the fixture; an 80-frame sub-family at a P105 pivot passes (W), blocks and (G) but fails (D), with an exact integer kernel certificate, so (G) does not imply (D) for arbitrary frame families; a first-frame control). verify.py --part i/3: per P105 unit the pivot is a live frame satisfying (D), (G), (W) and nonempty blocks, ranks modulo 1000003 as lower bounds; all 242802 pass (200 s wall, 1861 CPU-s on 10 Apple-silicon cores; the registered replay passes in 249 s wall). The criterion is PR1616's with bitmask rows and a different elimination order; it agreed with PR1616's implementation on 1200 random (unit, frame) pairs and 800 sub-family controls with (W), (G) and (D) failures (scratch check, not registered). make_units.py (which now finds pivots by exact search) reproduced both data files byte for byte from scratch, and checked that the orbit sizes sum to C(112,k) for k = 4..7 (census, not needed by the argument); its units and pivots match PR1616's unregistered search_p105.py run exactly. tally_earlier.py (unregistered, stdlib) reruns the exact criterion on all 17429 live frames preceding a pivot: 17210 fail (W), 219 fail nonempty blocks, none fail (G) or (D). Mutation controls on scratch copies (non-live pivot, (W)-failing pivot, one changed level-7 element index) each fail. A read-only OpenAI Codex review found no soundness defect. PR1560's Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 are cited, not re-proved.

open_questions.question: Do (D) and (G) hold at every pivot of a live set once (W) and nonempty blocks hold?
open_questions.why_it_matters: In the P107, P106 and P105 searches no frame passing (W) and nonempty blocks ever failed (G) or (D); a lemma would remove every rank computation and leave a counting check.
open_questions.first_step: control.g-without-d shows (G) alone does not force (D) for an arbitrary frame family, so a lemma must use that the family is all live frames. Search deeper deletions (P104 and below) for a pivot passing (W), nonempty blocks and (G) whose full live family fails (D).

open_questions.question: Does the masked rigidity route say anything for nine or more costly terms?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR1560's criterion and PR1212's model are for exactly eight costly terms; the rank-shape card needs masked supports that change an assumption of the eight-term bound.
open_questions.first_step: State the nine-term E-graph equations and check whether PR1560's identity (6) argument has an analogue.
open_questions.blocked_by: No nine-term rigidity statement exists to verify.
